title: Layering every technique in RAG, one query at a time - David Karam, Pi Labs (fmr. Google Search)

primary.label: Retrieval, Search & Knowledge
primary.rationale: The entire talk is a catalog of RAG/search techniques: in-memory retrieval, BM25, embeddings, rerankers, custom embeddings, ranking signals, and multi-backend recall.

secondary.label: Evaluation, Testing & Benchmarking
secondary.rationale: The frame is a quality-engineering loop: personal query-set bars, loss analysis, and empirical choice of the next technique.

secondary.label: AI Product, UX & Human Factors
secondary.rationale: The closer is product design under stochastic quality: high-promise vs degraded UI and human-in-the-loop escalation.

secondary.label: Agent Architecture & Harnesses
secondary.rationale: A substantial middle section is agent query orchestration, fan-out, and the LLM/search-engine control boundary.

domains.label: Search & Knowledge
domains.rationale: The subject is information retrieval and RAG quality for search-backed generation.

domains.label: Enterprise Operations
domains.rationale: Running examples are a CRM agent launch bar and email/CRM vertical semantics.

domains.label: Legal & Compliance
domains.rationale: The custom-embedding case study is legal vocabulary (regime, material, moot, regulations).

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The catalog is meant for any RAG product, with shopping and Google Search as general IR examples.

summary:
David Karam, co-founder of Pi Labs (ASR: Pyabs) after Google Search, frames RAG improvement as quality engineering rather than a debate about whether RAG is dead. Techniques exist to hit a product launch bar (example: a CRM agent) on easy/medium/hard query sets. The loop is baseline → loss analysis → pick from a catalog using difficulty vs impact. Stay lazy: if it is not broken, do not add BM25, vectors, or custom embeddings.

The catalog is ordered by when the previous method fails. (1) In-memory retrieval: stuff documents into the context window; NotebookLM is the five-doc case that needs no index. Failures: corpus too large or the model cannot attend. (2) BM25: term frequency, document length, term rarity; cheap and usually worth trying; fails on non-keyword information needs. (3) Relevance embeddings: handle paraphrase (iPhone battery life vs how long until I must charge) but miss exact keyword matching. (4) Cross-encoder rerankers: joint query–document scoring; too expensive for the full corpus so retrieve-then-rerank. (5) Custom embeddings: generic relevance is only a proxy. Harvey + LanceDB legal example: regime, material, moot, laws and regulations sit outside a general embedding vocabulary.

Ranking is not relevance. Shopping/Perplexity: “cheap gifts” then “$50 or more” still returned $15/$40 items—a price signal never entered query understanding or rank. Merchant popularity, listen counts, and PageRank (prominence / inbound graph, not semantics) are corpus-shape signals. Horizontal NL semantics are a tiny slice of a vertical (CRM, email, legal). After you model the domain, user preference (clicks, thumbs) still disagrees with your ranker; combine CTR prediction with relevance and structured signals into one score.

Agents add an impedance mismatch: the LLM invents queries the tuned search backend does not expect. Take control of orchestration: fan a complex ask into N narrower queries (Google AI Mode flashing 15–20). He likes MCP but does not believe prompting can teach the model the backend. Supplementary retrieval: search more backends for recall; an ambiguous “simple Middle Eastern dish” query stumped a 6,000-person Google Search org because food vs images intent is unclear.

At GPU/cost overload, distill a smaller model that holds the quality bar (Perplexity’s fast QA specialist; 10s vs 2s churn). When engineering still fails, punt to product/UX: human-in-the-loop support, or Google Shopping’s high-promise filter UI vs a degraded ten-blue-links list. Everything is empirical. Slides: pi.ai-talk. Close: talk RAG and the models they are building.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.
temporalContext: Transcript claims reflect the publication date; linked external context was checked at the run's research date.
takeaways: Treat RAG techniques as a quality-engineering toolbox ordered by difficulty and impact, not as a default architecture.
Baseline a personal query-set bar, analyze losses, then apply only the next cheaper method that addresses the failure.
The failure ladder is in-memory → BM25 → relevance embeddings → cross-encoder rerank → custom embeddings → extra ranking signals → preference.
Relevance is a proxy: price, merchant, popularity, and PageRank prominence are non-semantic ranking signals.
Agent tool-use often issues the wrong queries; fan-out and backend-aware orchestration beat hoping MCP teaches the search engine.
For recall, search more backends (supplementary retrieval) instead of over-optimizing a single call.
Distill when latency/cost, not quality, is the constraint; a large LLM is often overqualified.
When stochastic quality cannot hit 100%, change the product surface: degrade or escalate to a human.

organization.name: Pi Labs
organization.summary: Pi Labs Inc. (withpi) was an independent San Francisco company founded by David Karam and Achint Srivastava after Google Search. First-party and conference pages describe an applied AI evaluation and optimization product: application-specific scoring, synthetic data, prompt optimization, customized retrieval, and Pi Scorer. The public withpi.ai and build.withpi.ai hosts no longer resolve; the remaining first-party surface is the Hugging Face org titled Pi Labs Inc., which hosts a Pi Scorer cross-encoder model and retrieval-eval datasets. Accel and the AI Engineer speaker page record an acquisition by Microsoft after this July 2025 talk. Google, Harvey, LanceDB, NotebookLM, and Perplexity appear only as illustrations. Speaker employer at video time is Pi Labs.
organization.status: Acquired by Microsoft after the talk (Accel and conference bio). withpi.ai DNS is gone. Live first-party artifacts remain on huggingface.co/withpi. No evidence the featured implementation moved to a different company name.
